analysis.cia_basis: Controlled TSan proves owner data race/UB in the modeled component shape. Product crash/DoS, returned-entry integrity, confidentiality and privilege effects unmeasured.
analysis.conflicting_access_pair: SetInstance write at js_proxy.h:37 versus GetInstance read at :42 on the same owner; async close and sync result-set calls provide the call shape.
analysis.entry_privilege: Source-visible distributedKVStore NAPI entries; runtime permission, package resolution, app identity, cross-app/remote reachability and attacker control partial/unknown.
analysis.shared_object_lifecycle: napi_wrap owns the JS wrapper until finalize; async ContextBase keeps selfRef. GetInstance copies retain the pointee while SetInstance(nullptr) drops the wrapper owner. Owner control-block and pointee lifetime cross JS/worker contexts.
analysis.shared_ptr_publication_order: GetResultSet execute calls SetInstance; completion returns the wrapper. Sync methods copy GetInstance. CloseResultSet execute calls GetInstance then SetInstance(nullptr). Completion serialization does not order execute against a later sync JS call.
analysis.synchronization_protocol: No mutex/atomic owner API in JSProxy. NapiQueue serializes completion only. Fixed control uses a mutex; proposed minimal patch uses atomic_load/atomic_store.
analysis.thread_or_event_queue_ownership: Sync ResultSet methods use GetCbInfoSync on the NAPI/JS call context. GetResultSet/CloseResultSet use NapiQueue::AsyncWork: execute runs on the NAPI worker pool and complete on the JS/NAPI queue. The same JSProxy owner can be read by a sync call while async CloseResultSet clears it.
analysis.trigger_window: Source-visible sequence getResultSet -> closeResultSet -> immediate getEntry/getCount before async close execute completes. The controlled Harness models this exact overlap.

groups.classification_rationale: Real owner pair but unresolved queue, trigger, entry/privilege and CIA facts; retain unknown.
unknown_reasons: measured product CIA and stable exploitability

analysis.conflicting_access_pair: Getter/setter and direct read/write pairs exist; source-rect/reset readers do not alone prove a cross-thread same-object pair.
analysis.entry_privilege: Real PIP/window APIs source-visible; caller privilege, trust boundary, attacker control and deployment unknown.
analysis.shared_object_lifecycle: PIP/window manager and PipOption share controller shared_ptrs. Reset tears down attachment but does not establish synchronized owner publication/destruction for all fields.
analysis.shared_ptr_publication_order: Start copies main XComponentController from PipOption; reuse can replace it. SetXComponentController writes pipXComponentController_ and attaches it; ResetExtController detaches on stop. Source-rect/reset readers use the same members.
analysis.synchronization_protocol: No local lock/atomic owner API covers both controller members and observed access paths. Same-runner serialization is possible but unproven.
analysis.thread_or_event_queue_ownership: NAPI/ANI PIP methods and window lifecycle/source-rect/reset callbacks are visible, but all setter/reader paths are not bound to one event runner or proven serial queue; main and PIP controller paths may differ.
analysis.trigger_window: Concurrent Start/Update/Stop/SetX while main and PIP windows share a controller. No controlled product interleaving or runner trace.

analysis.cia_basis: No measured product crash, corruption, disclosure or privilege effect.
analysis.conflicting_access_pair: Lexical same-object ptrChannel_ write/read pair exists; concurrent overlap is plausible but unproven.
analysis.entry_privilege: Source-visible SoftBus device and remote-command paths; privilege, trust boundary and attacker control unknown.
analysis.shared_object_lifecycle: Manager map owns the executor. The posted runner captures weak_from_this and locks self while processing. Offline releases the channel and removes the map entry; GetExecutorChannel returns a channel shared_ptr by value. Channel retention is visible, but ptrChannel_ publication/reset order is unresolved.
analysis.shared_ptr_publication_order: GetOrCreateRemoteCommandExecutor publishes the executor; NotifyDeviceOnline checks GetChannel and calls SetChannel under RemoteCommandManager::mutex_. CreateChannelIfNeeded writes ptrChannel_ under RemoteCommandExecutor::recursive_mutex_; ProcessOneCommand/ExecuteRemoteCommand read it. Different locks leave no proven happens-before edge.
analysis.synchronization_protocol: Manager mutex covers map and manager wrapper; executor mutex covers buffering/CreateChannelIfNeeded. Public Get/SetChannel and several reads/writes are not covered by one lock. Protocol incomplete.
analysis.thread_or_event_queue_ownership: Send command work is posted to TokenSyncManagerService::GetSendEventHandler() on an FFRT EventRunner; device online/offline enters through SoftBus device callbacks and socket session callbacks. Exact callback thread identities and common serialization are not proven.
analysis.trigger_window: Device-online channel creation versus send-runner processing or socket callback use, with offline release/remove as a third event. Feasible product schedule and rate are not established.

groups.classification_rationale: Partial synchronization and incomplete reachability/impact evidence; retain unknown.
unknown_reasons: happens-before or controlled ptrChannel_ race/fixed run

VtpStreamSocket creates detached NotifyStreamListener/DoStreamRecv threads and invokes streamReceiver_ under streamSocketLock_. streamListener_ itself is not shown to be read by callbacks; StreamSocketListener keeps a separate listener_ copy.
analysis.trigger_window: Would require product caller to invoke public SetStreamRecvListener concurrently with Create*Channel or another setter. Production call-site search found setup calls and tests only.
